videos.title: Jang Dong-hyeok: “(The ruling party’s) Starbucks boycott will only last until June 3rd... The tar...
videos.subtitle_summary:
1. Jang Dong-hyeok predicts that the Starbucks boycott by the ruling party will last until June 3rd, suggesting they will return to Starbucks coffee after that date. In 2016, the Democratic Party held numerous shows against Samsung over SAR radiation concerns, but opposition to Samsung disappeared shortly after the presidential election. Moon Jae-in expressed support for Samsung just a month into his presidency.
2. In 2023, the Democratic Party campaigned on the issue of decommissioning the Haku Shirima nuclear power plant and mobilized the entire nation. After the general election in 2024, have you seen the Democratic Party talking about Haku Shirima? Moon Jae-in even negotiated with Japan over Haku Shirima seafood imports. The target of this election's campaign song is Starbucks. Moon Jae-in and his supporters are trying to channel public anger over the cancelled investigation and special prosecutor into Starbucks.
3. Jang Dong-hyeok calls for citizens to show their will for choosing their own coffee on Friday, suggesting this election is a battle between Moon Jae-in and the free people. He also criticizes those who use 5.18 (a significant date in South Korean history) as a shield for violence, such as Jeong Woon-ho and Song Young-gil of Gwangwon Province, and calls for their resignation.

videos.title: Starbucks 'Tank Day' event sparks political battle… Lee's criticism met with "election-geared ant...
videos.subtitle_summary: Starbucks 'Tank Day' event sparks political controversy over Lee Jae-myung's criticism of a marketing phrase. The controversy stems from Lee Jae-myung's anger over the use of a mug with a siren design, which was marketed in an event that took place on April 18th. Some believe this event was intentionally designed to evoke memories of the Sewol Ferry disaster, which occurred on April 16th, 2014. Critics argue that this is a disrespectful and insensitive marketing tactic, and are calling for Starbucks to apologize and reconsider their actions.
